mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in tightening periods than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within two months indicates a weakening labor market, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown and thus negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of rising unemployment (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consistent increase in housing starts over three consecutive months signals a strengthening demand for housing, which is a proxy for overall economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of increasing housing starts (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production by more than 1% over two months signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to increased prices and reduced corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of decreasing industrial production (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than GDP (GDPC1) over a quarter, it signals a shift in consumer spending that boosts corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > GDPC1 growth in 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher when RSAFS growth exceeds GDPC1 growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 over two months signals a weakening labor market, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown and thus negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of decreasing nonfarm payrolls (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% over two months signals inflationary pressure, which can lead to monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of increasing CPI (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year growth rate of real GDP (GDPC1) exceeds the growth rate of the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over a quarter, it signals real economic growth that boosts corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth > CPIAUCSL YoY growth in 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher when GDPC1 YoY growth exceeds CPIAUCSL YoY growth (t-test p > 0.05).
